candidates.definition_line: Same nature, different register — the edge of comparison
candidates.face_teaser: You rise to a contest. Comparison sharpens you, though it can also spend the energy you meant to keep. Put an equal in front of you and you find a gear you forgot you had. Just watch that the race doesn’t cost more than the finish line pays.
candidates.family_clause: the self the other four energies turn around

family_element.appetite: drive, contest, and the edge you sharpen against equals
family_element.notAlone: not pride alone, but the self the other four energies turn around

__ore.note: TG corpus — the K2 generation source (kept per REA_03 §2.4)

rulingRealm.phrase: Social Performance — the ego measured against its nearest competition
rulingRealm.desc: The part of a person that measures itself against others occupying the same territory. Not the internal standard of 比肩 but the comparative ego — what am I relative to the people most like me? The reference point is always lateral.

gifts: Genuine clarity about where the actual edges of capability lie — real peers reveal real limits
The competitive register sharpens rather than diminishes when healthy: you become more precisely what you are through the comparison
Socially intelligent in reading where they stand relative to those who actually matter to them
shadows: Resources spent measuring rather than building — the comparison can become the point
Collaboration with the people most similar is structurally the hardest relationship to sustain
Validation from genuine peers lands harder than victory over those who don't understand the territory
__ore.hiddenDynamic: Underneath the rivalry is a specific, rarely admitted desire: genuine recognition from exactly the people most like them. Not recognition from outsiders — that lands hollow. The need is for the specific peer who understands what the achievement cost to acknowledge it as real.

outputs.desc: Real peers show you where your actual limits lie, giving you a clarity others never get.
At its best the rivalry sharpens you — you become more precisely what you are by measuring against equals.
You read with unusual accuracy where you stand relative to the people who actually matter to you.

frictions.desc: Resources can get spent measuring rather than building, until the comparison quietly becomes the point.
Working with the people most like you is the relationship that's structurally hardest to sustain.
Validation from a true peer lands harder than any victory over those who don't understand the territory.

career.mechanism: 劫财 → lateral competition, peer performance benchmarking
career.text: Thrives in competitive environments where performance is measured against others — fields with visible rankings and clear standards. The comparison drive produces real results when channeled toward the work rather than toward the rival.

relationships.mechanism: 劫财 → rivalry with similar partners, resource contention
relationships.text: Most significant relationships are with people most similar to them. Sharing resources with someone in the same lane feels like giving something away. The specific challenge: genuine collaboration with the people who most deserve it.

wealth.mechanism: 劫财 → resource contention, competitive wealth dynamics
wealth.text: Resource contention with peers is a recurring pattern. The competitive orientation can produce genuine wealth when directed toward building rather than measuring. Risk: losing resources to rivalry.

health.mechanism: 劫财 → competitive overperformance, external calibration of limits
health.text: Competitive orientation produces overperformance relative to the body's actual capacity — pushing past physical limits to match or exceed a rival. The self-monitoring calibrates to the external reference rather than internal signals.
